facts.statement: Serge Modular was developed by Serge Tcherepnin in the early 1970s at the California Institute of the Arts; the first-generation modules (1972-73) used banana jacks and test cords on grid-like panels, and their paper-printed front panels gave the name 'paperface'.
The 1979 catalogue is quoted for the SSG, showing the original system was catalogued modules; no other original-era documents were read.

Random*Source sells licensed Serge designs: Paperface 50 (2 or 3 panels or single panels), 4U full panels with banana jacks (Mantra II, La Bestia III, Tantra, Yantra and others), 4x4 modules and Eurorack (3U) modules; panels run from +/-12 V.
facts.locator: Home page, Paperface page, Serge Panels page

facts.statement: Serge Tcherepnin joined Random*Source as Chief Innovation Officer in November 2018 to lead a 5th generation of the system; the Eurorack SSG is described as a licensed, authorised adaptation of the original design.
facts.locator: Home page news item; SSG product page

facts.statement: Random*Source also holds Jurgen Haible's electronic heritage since 2015, and the Serge name is a registered trademark.

The FAQ says Eurorack (3U, mini-jack, may normalise and carry 0 V ground) and classic 4U (banana jacks) use the same circuitry and voltage levels and can be patched together given a format jumbler (Pont Neuf) and a common ground.
facts.locator: FAQ, 'Eurorack vs 4U' and 'Can I mix' answers

facts.statement: Every 4U or Paperface system is built to order; DIY kits are suspended (apart from some Haible PCBs) because of the chip crisis.

Three signal families by jack colour: white for DC control voltages (typically 0 to +5 V, positive polarity), red for logic/trigger pulses in the same range, black for bipolar AC signals (audio and bipolar CV, bipolar CV typically +/-2.5 V). The manual says this is a recommendation, not a rule.
The whole system tolerates +/-12 V; voltages outside that range at any input or output may damage a module, and the system is meant for a linear +/-12 V PSU.
facts.locator: Manual sections 'Before you start' and 'Signal types'

facts.statement: Any voltage levels may be freely mixed in patching; connecting output to output or input to input should be avoided.
Pink, grey and other coloured jacks mark special functions, for example the sync input on the oscillator and the coupler of the SSG.

SSG (Smooth & Stepped Generator): a patch-programmed module with a Smooth section (slew, portamento, track-and-hold, cycling triangle LFO) and a Stepped section (sample-and-hold with slew limit, staircase waveforms), plus a Coupler comparing both outputs.

Paperface manual: the Coupler red output is a 0-5 V pulse, the black 'hot' Coupler output is bipolar up to -12 V to +12 V; in cycle mode the Smooth side makes a triangle from about 0 to 4-5 V and runs from below 1 Hz to about 4 kHz.
Random*Source Eurorack SSG: 18 HP, 35 mA at +12 V and 30 mA at -12 V, audio range up to 4 kHz, adds a bipolar Coupler output; also sold as SMT DIY kit with build docs.

NTO (New Timbral Oscillator): described by the maker as Serge's most ambitious oscillator; the Random*Source version replaces obsolete parts, adds a pulse output and an adjustable oven temperature, 18 HP Eurorack, EUR 555.
The page calls the NTO 'legendary' and says it combines raw vintage sound with astonishing precision; this is advertising language.

DSG (Dual Universal Slope Generator): unity-gain voltage followers with independently voltage-controlled rise and fall times, usable as envelope, LFO, portamento, envelope follower, pulse delay, divider or audio oscillator.

DSG mk2 for Eurorack improves tracking (up to 4 octaves) and speed, covers over 10 kHz in the top section, has separate rise and fall CV inputs and a 50% duty pulse out, with some temperature compensation in the new version.

Triple Waveshaper (Paperface): three identical sections that can be chained; an input is turned into a distorted version (e.g. triangle to a sine at 2F, saw to an approximate sine at 1F); two CV inputs per section; each section has a white unipolar (0-5 V) and a black AC-coupled bipolar output.

1973 Filter (Paperface): accepts AC signals and gives low-pass (12 dB/oct), high-pass (12 dB/oct) and fixed-bandwidth band-pass outputs around one frequency set by a knob and a CV input; resonance is knob-only (not voltage controlled); can act as a sine oscillator; a separate section converts a banana-jack audio signal to a balanced TRS output.
facts.locator: Manual section '1973 Filter (VCF) and Balanced Output'

facts.statement: Paperface VCO (2022 revision of the 1973 oscillator): simultaneous saw and sine-like waves, each unipolar and bipolar; 1 V/Oct input with temperature compensation, up to 2 more CV inputs with attenuverters, wave-shape CV, sync inputs; VCO+ adds PWM pulse out, white/pink noise and the classic S/H source.
Systems are patched with banana jacks and cords (the 1970s originals used test cords); the FAQ confirms 4U panels use banana jacks. No patch memory or recall is documented in the pages read.
Sequencing is itself patch-programmed: Paperface 50 includes sequencer/programmer and gate sequencer modules and a metronomic clock (contents listed, not read in detail).

Paperface VCO provides a temperature-compensated 1 V/Oct input and sync inputs; the Yantra panel has an FX Interface for external pedals and processors; a balanced TRS output exists on the 1973 filter section.
facts.locator: Manual 'Oscillator (VCO)', '1973 Filter'; Serge Panels page, Yantra description

facts.statement: Serge Eurorack and 4U share signal levels and can be combined via the Pont Neuf format jumbler with a common ground (all R*S PSUs include a banana ground jack).
facts.locator: FAQ 'Can I mix Eurorack Serge and 4U Serge?'

facts.statement: A Touch Activated Keyboard (TKB) is sold for Paperface and Eurorack; MIDI or digital control interfaces are not mentioned in the pages read.
